For k distinct value blocks, atomic R records which block is least in each triple; the counts binom(k-i,2) distinguish all blocks except the top two, whose swap changes no atomic relation. Thus every k>=2 qf class contains exactly two complete orders, while the constant class is singleton, giving (F_n+1)/2. The order relation gives a binary homogeneous expansion; transitivity makes every parameter-free unary relation trivial, so unary additions cannot homogenize the nonhomogeneous reduct.
